global_layoffs.description: eBay reportedly plans to eliminate about 9% of its workforce, or approximately 1,000 roles, in a second 2026 reduction aimed at streamlining operations amid technology investment.
Barclays disclosed plans to cut about 5,000 jobs, citing organisational simplification and technology-change efficiency driven by AI, with roughly 60% of reductions in support functions.
Kroger plans to eliminate about 3,000 corporate roles over three years while expanding artificial-intelligence use across the grocery business.
Meta announced a workforce reduction of about 10% as it increases AI infrastructure spending and hires specialised AI talent.
FICO planned to eliminate approximately 15% of its workforce while simplifying its operating structure and expanding AI workflows in product development.
DNB reportedly planned a reduction of about 400 positions as it redirects spending toward AI and operational efficiency.
HSBC announced plans to remove about 20,000 roles, or roughly 10% of its workforce, as part of an AI overhaul.
Amazon announced 16,000 corporate job cuts in an AI- and efficiency-driven restructuring.

gulf_mena_automation.description: A company study found that 82% of surveyed GCC consumer-economy professionals use AI daily or weekly, highlighting rapid workplace adoption but limited confidence in effective use.

A regional workforce study reported that 22% of GCC respondents had already combined roles because of AI and 41% were exploring further consolidation across technical, administrative and customer-service functions.

saudi_policy_updates.title: Localization of supporting administrative professions
saudi_policy_updates.description: Saudi Arabia brought a decision requiring 100% localization of supporting administrative professions in the private sector into force.
saudi_policy_updates.source: Saudi Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development

ai_workforce_signals.headline: GCC AI use is widespread but workforce confidence lags
ai_workforce_signals.description: An Al-Futtaim study found that 82% of surveyed GCC consumer-economy professionals use AI daily or weekly, while only 39% feel very or extremely confident using it. The gap points to substantial near-term demand for AI training and workflow redesign in Gulf employers.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: GCC employers shift from job elimination to role consolidation
ai_workforce_signals.description: A regional study reported that 22% of respondents had already combined roles because of AI and 41% were actively exploring consolidation. Technical testing, code-cleanup, reporting, finance processing and customer-service tasks were among the functions most exposed.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Barclays links workforce reduction to AI efficiency
ai_workforce_signals.description: Barclays said planned cuts of about 5,000 jobs were tied partly to organisational simplification and technology-change efficiency driven by AI. Support functions, including development roles, account for most of the planned reductions.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: eBay announces second workforce reduction of 2026
ai_workforce_signals.description: eBay reportedly plans to remove about 1,000 positions, equivalent to 9% of its workforce. The reduction reflects continuing operational streamlining as large technology companies redirect resources toward automation and AI-enabled productivity.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI-linked layoffs extend across banking and retail
ai_workforce_signals.description: A Reuters factbox identified AI-linked workforce reductions across banks, retailers, technology companies and industrial firms, including HSBC, Amazon, Standard Chartered, Microsoft and Kroger. The spread indicates that AI-related restructuring is no longer confined to software companies.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Meta trades non-AI roles for AI infrastructure and talent
ai_workforce_signals.description: Meta’s reported reduction of roughly 8,000 roles coincides with increased spending on AI infrastructure and recruitment of specialised AI employees. The pattern reflects a shift from broad headcount growth toward targeted AI capability investment.

weekly_stats.notable_trend: AI-related workforce restructuring is broadening beyond technology into banking, retail and administrative functions, while GCC employers increasingly consolidate roles and face a pronounced gap between frequent AI use and employee confidence.
